weakest1_debounce-function.issue: Original prompt used '<T extends unknown[]>' which is a poor/unidiomatic generic constraint. Prompt also lacked structure and examples. Additionally, the task ran last and hit Gemini daily rate limit (free tier: 20 req/day).
weakest1_debounce-function.improvement: Rewrote with idiomatic generic '<F extends (...args: never[]) => unknown>', added explicit requirements for leading/trailing options, cancel/flush methods, this-binding passthrough, and a comprehensive few-shot example showing the full implementation pattern.
weakest1_debounce-function.expectedImpact: Should eliminate the type-constraint confusion and produce valid TypeScript with proper export and all required identifiers.

weakest2_data-fetcher-hook.issue: Generated code failed validSyntax check despite being syntactically plausible — likely a template-literal vs brace-counting false positive. Original prompt was terse with no structure guidance.
weakest2_data-fetcher-hook.improvement: Added explicit requirements for state shape, cleanup logic, AbortError handling, initial state values, and a full few-shot example. Added file extension guidance (.ts not .tsx) and explicit JSON output format instruction.
weakest2_data-fetcher-hook.expectedImpact: Should produce consistently well-structured code that passes all syntax checks.

weakest3_login-form.issue: Passed all formal checks but generated code had security issues: logged password to console and used alert() for success feedback. Original prompt focused only on validation, not production quality.
weakest3_login-form.improvement: Added explicit security requirements (never log credentials, never use alert()), added specific email regex, per-field error display instructions, clear-error-on-resubmit pattern, try/catch requirement, and a few-shot example of the validate function signature.
weakest3_login-form.expectedImpact: Should produce production-quality code without security anti-patterns while still passing all checks.

benchmarkConfigChanges.addedGeminiProvider: Added direct Gemini (gemini-2.5-flash) support via @google/genai SDK as primary provider, with VibeServe HTTP as fallback. Provider selected via BENCHMARK_LLM_PROVIDER env var.
benchmarkConfigChanges.addedEnvLoading: Auto-loads GEMINI_API_KEY from Mutly-Daemon-Agent/.env for zero-config runs from reporank workspace.
benchmarkConfigChanges.addedRateLimitDelay: Added 4-second inter-task delay to handle Gemini free-tier rate limits.
benchmarkConfigChanges.addedFewShotExamples: All three improved prompts now include few-shot TypeScript examples guiding correct output structure.

reRunStatus: Blocked by Gemini free-tier quota exhaustion (20 req/day limit for gemini-2.5-flash). The VibeServe OpenCode provider also failed (CLI timeout). Re-run will succeed once quota resets or a paid API key is configured.
instructions: To re-run: ensure GEMINI_API_KEY is set in Mutly-Daemon-Agent/.env, then: cd reporank/apps/cli && tsx src/codegen-benchmark.ts --output ../../benchmark-results-codegen-v2.json
